title: Volumes in Compose
idea: In Compose you declare a named volume once, under a top-level `volumes` key, then mount it into services by name.
points: Compose prefixes the volume with the project name, such as `bookstore_pgdata`.
A service mounts it as `NAME:CONTAINER_PATH` under its own `volumes` key.
A path starting with `./` makes a bind mount of a host folder instead.
To share a volume, list it under each service's `volumes` key.

hero.caption: Only `-v` removes volumes. Compose never deletes a bind-mounted host folder.

code.title: compose.yaml
code.caption: Two named volumes and one bind mount. Assume the API saves covers and reads settings.

walk.text: `./config` is a bind mount, resolved from the folder holding `compose.yaml`. `:ro` is read-only.
Database files go in `pgdata`. Postgres 18 and later keep data under `/var/lib/postgresql`.
Declare each named volume once at the top level. An empty entry uses default settings.

code.title: Keep and delete
code.caption: Set `DB_PASSWORD` in `.env` first. The data survives `down`; `down -v` removes it.

walk.text: Start the project. Compose creates `covers` and `pgdata`, prefixed with the project name.
Remove the containers and the network. The volumes stay.
Start again. The database finds its files in `pgdata`.
Remove containers, network and named volumes. The data is gone.

pitfalls: `down -v` deletes named volumes and their data for good; add `-v` only to reset.
Check your image's data path. Postgres 18+ mounts `/var/lib/postgresql`; 17 and earlier, `/var/lib/postgresql/data`.
`POSTGRES_PASSWORD` only applies to an empty volume; it will not change an existing database's password.

quiz.q: After `docker compose down -v`, you run `docker compose up -d`. What does `db` start with?
options: The old data, restored from the image
The old data, because volumes are permanent
An empty database; `down -v` deleted the volume
An error: the volume no longer exists
quiz.why: `-v` removes the named volumes. `up` declares a new, empty `pgdata`, so Postgres initializes a fresh database.

takeaway: Named volumes survive `down`; only `down -v` deletes their data.
